title: Thompson (1917) Ch. XIV — Leaf/floret divergence and Fibonacci parastichies
citation: Thompson, D.W. (1917). On Growth and Form, Chapter XIV: On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis, pp. 635-651, Figs. 325-327.
claim_text: Leaf/floret divergence approximates the golden (Fibonacci) angle (~137.5 deg), with rational approximations 1/2, 1/3, 2/5, 3/8... and Fibonacci numbers of parastichies.

state_variables.alpha: divergence angle between successive primordia (degrees or radians)

boundary_conditions.capitulum_disk: primordia on planar disk r <= R_max
boundary_conditions.rising_phyllotaxis: outer rim pair transitions (m,n) -> (n, m+n) along Fibonacci sequence

empirical_claims: Sunflower capitulum florets show divergence near 137.5 deg
Visible parastichy spirals follow Fibonacci numbers (e.g. 34 and 55)
Rational fractions 1/2, 1/3, 2/5, 3/8 approximate the golden turn

modern_validation_refs.note: Swinton et al. (2016) Helianthus parastichy survey
